title: Chiral Parafermions in Floquet $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Topological Order
authors: Melissa Will, Harald Schmid, Jan Egger, Adam Gammon-Smith, Michael Knap, Frank Pollmann
abstract: Floquet topological order (FTO) extends topology beyond equilibrium, giving rise to phenomena, such as the dynamical transmutation of anyons. Here, we realize $\mathbb{Z}_N$ FTO in a generalized Kitaev honeycomb model with clock degrees of freedom using a three-step periodic drive. The driven system admits an emergent description in terms of constrained parafermions coupled to conserved $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields. At the boundary, the drive generates chiral parafermionic Floquet edge modes. We resolve their propagation through correlation functions, characterize their fractional quantum-information transport through the radical chiral unitary index, and use their dynamics to probe exchange statistics. In the bulk, we explore the dynamical anyon transmutation with a non-equilibrium loop order parameter. At a Floquet sweet spot, where the drive becomes Clifford, these phenomena can be accessed using stabilizer simulations. Short-time matrix-product-state simulations away from this point show that the chiral edge response persists at accessible times. Our results establish $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Kitaev models as a setting for exploring intrinsically non-equilibrium topological phenomena on qudit-based quantum processors.
summary: This work investigates $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Floquet Topological Order using a driven Kitaev model on qudits. The authors show that the drive generates robust chiral parafermionic edge modes and induces anyonic time crystal behavior in the bulk. This establishes the model as a promising platform for studying non-equilibrium topological physics on quantum processors.
main_problem: The paper explores realizing and characterizing $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Floquet Topological Order (FTO) in a non-equilibrium setting, extending beyond the well-studied $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case.
main_result: They demonstrate that the driven Kitaev model generates chiral parafermionic edge modes and exhibits bulk dynamics characterized by anyonic time crystal behavior.
method: The study combines theoretical mapping (Fradkin-Kadanoff-type) with advanced numerical simulations, including Matrix-Product States (MPS) and stabilizer formalisms.
model_or_system: The system is a generalized Kitaev honeycomb model incorporating clock degrees of freedom (qudits), driven periodically by a three-step Floquet drive.
key_observables: Chiral parafermionic edge modes, dynamical anyon transmutation (tracked by a non-equilibrium loop order parameter), and the radical chiral unitary index quantifying information flow.
important_parameters: The system exhibits distinct regimes, notably the 'Clifford point' where the drive simplifies, and the general non-equilibrium dynamics away from this point.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to constrained parafermions and uses MPS simulations, which are limited by rapid entanglement growth away from the Clifford point.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the action of clock operators, the honeycomb lattice structure, the mapping contour, and the evolution of conserved $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge links.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ FTO model, mapping it to parafermions, analyzing the dynamics of string operators and anyons, and finally simulating the edge and bulk properties in different parameter regimes.
why_interesting: The focus on Floquet engineering of topological order, particularly using qudits and parafermions, provides a concrete theoretical framework for designing quantum simulators for exotic non-equilibrium phases.
